## Summary

mlx-rs is a Rust workspace that provides bindings and high-level abstractions over Apple's MLX machine learning framework, targeting Apple Silicon hardware. The repository is organized into several crates: the core `mlx-rs` crate (published as `pmetal-mlx-rs`) exposes tensor operations, neural network layers (convolutions, attention/transformer components, activation functions, normalization layers, linear layers, embedding, recurrent cells), automatic differentiation via a gradient computation API, and device/memory management backed by the MLX C++ library via FFI. Supporting crates include `mlx-internal-macros` (procedural macros used internally for code generation and derive traits within the workspace), `mlx-lm` (utilities for loading language model weights, typically from Hugging Face safetensors/GGUF formats), and `mlx-lm-utils` (tokenizer support for language model inference). Runnable example binaries demonstrate end-to-end workflows: LLM inference using Mistral and Qwen3 architectures, and MNIST digit classification training. Externally, at least two downstream consumers are visible in the cross-repository dependency graph: a project named `inference` (which makes very heavy use of mlx-rs APIs across hundreds of call sites, strongly suggesting it is a standalone LLM inference application or service built on this library) and a project named `LensWorks` (which calls into mlx-rs across roughly 30 sites, suggesting a vision or image-processing application). The repository itself depends on the native MLX framework (Apple's C++/Metal ML library), linked via a build script, and on standard Rust ecosystem crates for serialization, tokenization, and numeric operations.

## Projects

### mlx-rs

mlx-rs is a Rust binding and high-level wrapper for Apple's MLX machine learning framework, providing neural network primitives (convolution layers, transformer components, activation functions), automatic differentiation utilities, and example applications for running language models (Mistral, Qwen3) and training on MNIST. The repository is organized as a workspace containing the core mlx-rs crate (published as pmetal-mlx-rs), supporting utility crates for language model tokenization (mlx-lm-utils) and model loading (mlx-lm), internal procedural macros (mlx-internal-macros), and runnable examples that demonstrate inference and training workflows on Apple Silicon hardware.
